ios.desc:
Meizo (明像) ⟶ « Clear image »

No ads. No sign-up. No notifications.
Just you and your documents.


■ MEIZO DESCRIPTION


Some scanners feel bloated or intrusive.
Meizo does only what you want:
It lets you scan your documents quickly, cleanly, and privately.
Just like your camera app does for your photos.

No accounts. No cloud storage. No hidden surprises.

Designed with a simple, vintage-inspired interface, Meizo helps you focus on what matters:
capturing your documents with speed and clarity.


■ WHAT ABOUT YOUR PRIVACY?


I believe privacy is a fundamental human right.

That’s why I designed Meizo from the ground up without any external frameworks.
There are no ads, no data mining, and nothing you scan is ever stored or shared.
Everything stays on your device, just as it should.

Simple. Honest. Yours.


■ ABOUT THE PRICE


Most scanner apps on the App Store rely on weekly or monthly subscriptions.

With Meizo, you can download the app and try it for free.
If you like it, you can pay once and use it for life.
$19.99. No subscriptions. Simple.

An optional annual subscription is also available for $9.99/year.


■ HOW CAN YOU HELP ME?


Since I don’t collect any data, your feedback means everything.

Feel free to email me at julien@lacroix.dev for suggestions, bugs, or just to say hello.
I personally read and reply to every email.



**********

■ MEIZO PRO

- Unlimited export
- Support an indie developer.


**********

quotes.text:
I’m an indie iOS developer and I built a small tool because I couldn’t find a simple, fast, privacy-respecting document scanner on the App Store.

Most scanners today require an account, upload files to their cloud, or push subscriptions aggressively. I wanted something that opens instantly, works offline, exports clean PDFs, and doesn’t track anything.

So I made Scan.

It opens as fast as the Camera app, processes documents locally, and doesn’t require an account. The design is inspired by the older, simpler iOS UI from the iOS 6 era because I’ve always liked how clean and fast it felt.

I’d love feedback, especially from other developers:
– Is the interaction flow intuitive enough?
– Does the “privacy-first + old-school design” direction make sense in 2025?
– Anything obviously missing for a 1.0?

Happy to answer questions.
